decision.result: the exact transformer synthesis is algebraically mild in component ratios but worst-case ill-conditioned in the recorded 24-channel coordinates
decision.requiredCommissioning: measure and invert the complete 24-port matrix with uncertainty propagation; do not infer the charging metric from nominal component tolerances
mitigations: search GL(24,Z)-equivalent Leech bases that jointly reduce conditioning, transformer density and interaction locality
calibrate the realized matrix and digitally or parametrically compensate coherent errors
target only the experimentally occupied spectral subspace and certify the resulting isometry
include parasitic modes in the measured admittance model rather than treating them as independent scalar tolerances
decision.rejectionRule: a nominal transformer bill of materials without a full-matrix spectral certificate is insufficient for Gate A provenance

established: the recorded exact K basis has two-norm condition number about 3.18e4, making sub-part-per-million relative matrix control sufficient for a one-percent worst-case inverse-metric guarantee
boundary: The bound is sufficient and adversarial, not a prediction of typical fabrication error. Congruent GL(24,Z) bases change Euclidean conditioning, structured errors may be less damaging, calibration may compensate them, and physical observables need not require uniform accuracy over all 24 eigen-directions.
